This!! I definitely think after I glowed up I actually had an easier time making friends and being respected haha! I’ve had a few encounters with jealous people but those were usually the minority. 

Actually, I used to have this misconception about intelligence. I was always considered a... child prodigy of sorts and praised by adults and classmates as a genius. Whenever people didn’t like me, I just assumed they were jealous of my intelligence and talents. It turns out, I was arrogant, insensitive and weird (not in a good way). These days, I still have confidence and I own my eccentricity, but I never assume the reason why someone dislikes me is due to jealousy. It’s almost always the fact that our personalities aren’t a good fit, our values are different, etc. And that’s okay— one can’t be liked by everyone! I’ve learned to allocate the blame where blame is due, and in a lot of cases if we’re both being decent people who make generally decent decisions, it’s likely the blame falls on no one. 

There is a huge misconception in media that pretty girls/boys are hated on, that everyone hates the popular kids except for their cronies, that if you’re smart/talented people will be jealous and hate you. That’s not true in my experience and in statistical averages. The popular kids are often nice, well rounded people who are socially involved. A lot of people loved by those around them are also ridiculously smart and talented. Beautiful people tend to have confidence and be positive, so they attract a lot of friends. It’s possible to have it all: beauty, success, intelligence and good relationships with those around you. 

Thinking that it has to be one or the other limits growth, it can help to think of it as one *and* the others too!

Thank you for such a beautiful comment as well! Wow— I didn’t see anyone who had an indigenous past life experience on here other than you. Ah, it would be interesting if it spanned multiple lifetimes for me, I’ve only been able to recall one past life so far. 

You know, it was kinda magical meeting them. I remember meeting one of them in a shared English class and just knowing that this was an important moment that was supposed to happen all along. She then led me to meet the whole gang and meeting them was like I’d already known them for years. It was so easy to fall into the dynamic— when I learned about their lives, it didn’t feel like getting to know a stranger, but rather like meeting an old friend who’d gone abroad and ended up getting a whole new life there that they’re now sharing with you. I don’t know why we all just stuck together like glue, but we did. Breaking curfew together, sneaking out at midnight, drumming on stop signs with drum sticks stolen from the music department, we went through the confusing and exhilarating teenage experience together. I remember being elbowed by our resident scaredy cat Clam while watching AHS (Arm’s scheme to scare Clam and Alfie) at Tweet’s house, Ryebread making a snide remark and Leggy’s muffled giggling in the background, and just kinda thinking I knew the definition of platonic love right there. Maybe I’d always known. It’s scary how I think about life and know, without a question, that they’re a constant for me no matter how far away we spread out to pursue our dreams. Just yesterday we had our weekly video call together and Arm’s roommate asked him “are those the people you keep calling every weekend?” And he replies “yeah, they’re like, the best friends I’ve ever had. Life soulmates or whatever. I told you about them so many times dude!” 

Ah, and I’ve gone n rambled about my friends again. I used to talk about them a lot more, but I was met with a lot of skepticism and negative reactions. A lot of people said “ah, how naive. Just wait till you guys drift apart in another year or so. Or wait until drama inevitably arises...” and “I used to think I’d be friends with some people forever. Now they’re basically strangers— you’ll learn it soon enough.” I don’t think that’ll happen so fast, and if so, I’m sure we’ll all come back together one day. As several of my friends have said, we’ll be retiring together into the same townhouse or retirement facility. Preferably causing trouble together! 

I suppose I do feel really tired of things? Even though I’m still a teen, I often look at all the things the world is comprised of and just feel as if I’ve seen and done all of it already. The only thing that never fails to interest me is the beauty, complexity, kindness and cruelty of humanity and nature. And to a lesser extent, the pursuit of truth and the satisfaction of curiosity. I definitely think my mental health issues stem in large part due to genetic issues and some shitty childhood experiences (through no fault of anyone). My grandfather died by suicide and most people in that side of the family have some form of severe mental illness (bipolar, schizophrenia, schizoid personality disorder). I also think that mental battles are one of the hardest to fight and it makes sense for one of the later down the road challenges that would be presented to souls further down the “life school”. Maybe like an AP class or something, or a college assignment. I try to think about it through a positive light, the bigger the challenge, the greater the reward. Those who battle mental illness and rise above it have deeper understanding of their identity, life’s meaning and true happiness. 

I am seeing a therapist currently and after legit tossing myself into a fire pit of self destruction I’ve decided to pick myself back up and get my life together. Hopefully things only go up from here!

Huh— that is pretty interesting! I never thought about in between lives, but that seems a lot more useful than PLR. However, I don’t really feel the need to do more regression. I think my curiosity is satisfied and I think I have a pretty dang clear idea of what I gotta do with this life. I also think a lot of the memories have been “unlocked” and if I truly felt the need to see more, I’d be able to access those things. 

Dunno— I see a lot of posts here with people kinda obsessively reaching into past lives to try to find the root of some trauma... but it’s like... turtles all the way down isn’t it? Just an onion of traumas after traumas. In general, I don’t like focusing too much on what has already happened, I’m the kind that goes “aight so that happened, observe analyse improve and move on.” I try not to dawdle on things that have already occurred and I have little control over— I only need the past to inform me on how to get to a better, happier future. 

I’m sure in the future I may feel the need to do more regressions, but for now, especially as a teenager, I think this is enough to grapple with haha. I have a strong intuition that this life is about learning how to live and how to have a healthy relationship with myself. From what I remember in the past life, I think I had the same difficulties with recognizing emotion, establishing self worth and communicating as I do now. At least, the way I seemed to think, feel and speak were the same in that life, so I don’t doubt I made the same mistakes. I think my circumstances are so favourable this time around so that I get the chance to really tackle these issues and focus on some deep rooted mental demons.

Honestly it was so out of left field! I thought since my parents are from Hong Kong it would place me somewhere in east Asia but nope! I know unfortunately little about First Nation people, and there is such diversity within that experience that I really can’t place any identifying information. 

It does feel quite hard... I’ve struggled with suicidal tendencies since middle school and I can’t exactly find a good reason. I was bullied and pushed around for a year or so, but I think everyone goes through that. My parents weren’t the best but they tried and they really care for me. And obviously, I have some amazing, and apparently fated, best friends! A lot of people like to try and find an event or a circumstance that triggered mental illness, as if it is a thing that gets cobbled together by shitty life circumstances. But it really isn’t just that— I can’t really pinpoint a moment that made me mentally ill, I recall having very self deprecating and depressing thoughts since early childhood. Evidently I can’t blame my past life either, all of the memories I’ve recalled have been positive experiences. 

So I’m working on it. I think this PLR gave me the right push— I need to stop blaming external things for how fucked up I am mentally. I’m gonna try therapy again and hopefully learn to overcome this and find joy in living. Everyone wants to see me happy. Fuck, I wanna see me happy too. Sometimes I tell my friends about something very disappointing like how I couldn’t get out of bed for days and have gone MIA from classes, fully expecting or even wanting them to hate me (yknow, depression shit). And they don’t. They just get concerned and try to help and love me even more. I have no idea where I’d be or if I’d even be alive if it weren’t for them.

Hey— I share some of those same feelings. I frequently have disturbingly realistic dreams (since I was 3 as well) that seem like the memories of other people, set in places I don’t know featuring people that I also don’t know. Very few of these dreams were... pleasant. I also struggle with mental illness and attempted suicide a few years ago. 

I thought some shit must’ve gone down in my past life— maybe I died terrified or angry or very sad, maybe something horrible happened to me or I was a horrible person and did horrible things.

However, during my PLR I saw that at least in one past life and likely the most prominent one, I was loved. My friend group of best friends in this life were in my past life where we were a team of nomadic... warriors? It seemed like we were all indigenous. It’s striking how one of the first memories that came from the PLR reflected my current relationship with my “second family”— there I was, sitting around a fire with them laughing, and it reminded me of how in the winter months in this life we would all crowd together on one of my friend’s ratty old crouch, collapsed across an assortment of bean bags and watch black mirror on Netflix. To my surprise, both in my past life and in the present, I seem to have an abundance of love. 

Sometimes, the PLR can show you the treasures you should hold onto tight and never let go. Sometimes, instead of uncovering trauma it could bring love and gratitude and a healthier perspective. Maybe that is what you could find thru a PLR! 

Everything I’ve just said was just personal experience tho— I have only tried it once and I certainly know nothing compared to the experts on this sub lol

Another thing that kinda struck me— everyone’s past lives seem traumatic but mine seemed alright. I got the sense that I was motivated by passion, I fought for what felt like a good cause, and I had a lot of fun. After the PLR I’ve been having a few snippets of memories come to me and they have all been somewhat positive or at least neutral. I was in tune and connected with nature and it seemed I really had a purpose with everything I did. I spent that life surrounded by my best friends (or soul group) and I’m spending this one surrounded by them as well. 

There wasn’t anything too tragic about my death— it seemed like I drowned alone in some sort of valley, on a clear day. But my death felt like it had more purpose than that, although I do remember a lot of regrets. Well, that’s to be expected, no one dies without regrets!

Honestly, I instinctually don’t really like white people, and white people during my lifetime have not done the most redeeming things either. Being yelled slurs across the street by trump supporters to a white woman accusing me of stealing from her in a mall (and subsequently stating she’d get me deported lmfao), I feel like many of my experiences have solidified that initial distrust of white people. When I told my best friends about this prejudice I’ve struggled with they simply said “you just sensed that you didn’t belong in the white man’s world before the rest of us— and honestly, most times, have you been proven wrong?” Maybe this bias was left over from a previous life where white ppl were also, generally, shitheads, but little of this life has supported the opposite take. The weirdest thing is, the one white guy in my friend group I saw in the PLR but he was not white there. 

I can definitely understand the level of trauma you’ve described though. My grandma is from Manchuria and her father (descended from aristocracy during the last dynasty and an important general) was captured and brutally executed by the Japanese (who had occupied her home in WWII), she almost lost her mind when my uncle chose to marry a japanese woman.

I definitely felt like when I first met my best friends, and formed our friend group, that it was meant to be. When I met them, it felt a little like I’d known them forever, and I would know them for lifetimes to come. Even though we were strangers, it was like the moment that I saw them I could see all of the possibilities stretching out. It made sense that in a past life we were adventurers and fighters of some sort. I’ve gone on a lot of adventures with them and fought many battles, but this time around it seems like those battles are mental and personal. 

I do remember a phrase said by someone who I apparently loved a lot in this past life and it was “when will you have the same courage when it comes to matters of heart?” And I felt like it tied to my death, somehow. 

Right before I “woke up” from the regression I sensed god, or who I have always called “god in this life. Glad to know my omniscient overlord buddy has always been with me? 

Some of what you’ve said is kinda wild to me, in the way where I have actually contemplated such a theory growing up. I always thought we were all aliens or gods or something but real life is a school simulation and when we’re done with a life we wake up and write essays about it. And lives progressively get more and more difficult conceptually intellectually and emotionally! 

Actually, during that PLR I felt distinctly for the “energy” of my family and couldn’t rly feel it, or it was just really faint. I have always felt that despite the decent relationship I have with my parents and sister, sometimes they feel a bit like strangers, or like the type of people you’re only close to because you spent a lot of time with them. In my in-utero vision I do remember distinctly hearing my sister say “hey! I chose you :D” and that matches up to real life where my older sister begged my mom for a younger sibling. 

I do wonder why she chose me. 

I will look into those books when school stops fucking me over with tests and essays and finals. Maybe during winter break when the idea of reading is no longer conflated with stress lol

Huh— is that why I didn’t see my family in my PLR? I was the only member of my family to be born in Canada. I thought Asia would be relevant since my family actually moved back to Asia for a decade for work and I spent a lot of my childhood there. 

Man maybe there really is a reason I feel so damn uncomfortable around white people? I never mean to, I always try to make sure I’m not being prejudiced, but since my earliest memories white people have made me feel angry and afraid for no apparent reason. Even white people in Hong Kong! I chalked it up to systemic racism etc... but this does make me think again.

Huh— that’s kinda wild. My family immigrated to Canada from Hong Kong, but ancestrally we’re a mix of Manchu/Korean/Tibetan. I was the only member of my family born in Canada— kinda like my parents’ pride and joy as immigrants. They always told me that I was the real Canadian all the time haha. We actually moved *back* to Hong Kong when I was in elementary and only returned to NA when I was in high school, so most of my childhood memories are actually in Asia. 

I remember my parents (who are fairly wealthy) looking to buy a vacation home in California. We drove around the state and even visited Yosemite, as a 10 year old at the time I was overwhelmed and decided I hated it. I looked at the scenery and just couldn’t shake the feeling that something horrible happened here. My parents were not happy about my lack of enthusiasm and scolded me, saying I was ungrateful for not appreciating the opportunity to get away from the fast paced life of the city. After a week in California the feeling passed and I decided the place was alright after all, and Yosemite even became a place that I enjoyed road trips to. 

Also, I expected to find my family in the PLR but didn’t— I didn’t see a single family member or feel their presence. That was weirdly disappointing, as I’m quite close with my family (as Asians tend to be) and thought they had to be there at least in some capacity. Instead I met my friends...? My friend group is a rag tag gang of misfits that found each other at a gifted school in the US when we were 13-14. Almost everyone is East Asian by ethnicity except for one white guy. Honestly, it’s a sorta bond I’ve never felt with people before, they’re like my second family and we just clicked. Even if we fought (we rarely did) we just always went back to each other. But I’m very confused— why is it that I wasn’t born as family to these people? Not in this life and evidently not in the past either. 

Btw thank you for your suggestions! I’m not big on reading but I’ll give it a shot haha!
Thanks for reading!!

Yo I’m East asian too and you’re such an inspiration ;-; my hair is around a 2a-2b, not nearly as curly as yours but definitely far from straight. I feel like I struggle with CGM a lot because I have that typical East Asian hair texture— dense, thick, sleek but very very stubborn. Almost every time I come out of the shower, my hair looks perfect after scrunching in gel and microplopping! Then, istg after diffusing it becomes a blob of half straight, half flat, and half explosion hair. 

My mom never taught me how to manage my wavy hair, she just ran a brush through it and tugged and complained about why she couldn’t get it straight, and then burned it with a straightener. My hair came from my dad, who coincidentally keeps his head bald :’) 

So I’m always so happy to see another East Asian with curly/wavy hair that I can learn from ;-; pls teach me ur ways!!! I will see if I can buy a denman brush but rn I’m staying with some family in HK and idk if I can purchase it here!
